prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1234; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed collision in the parking lot of a retail store while backing out of a space. Other vehicle was a parked sedan with minor rear bumper contact. Claimant states she felt dizzy and had a headache immediately after impact and was evaluated at an urgent care clinic the same day. Diagnosis noted as concussion. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Advised her of the claims process and requested medical records and the clinic's itemized bill.

Entry 2: Spoke again with claimant regarding her injury. She reports ongoing headaches, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating at work. She has not yet followed up with a neurologist and says her primary care physician has recommended rest and a return visit in two weeks. Reminded claimant that she may seek her own medical care and that we will review bills as they are submitted. Recorded her availability for a recorded statement.

Entry 3: Recorded statement taken from claimant. She confirms the sequence of events and that her vehicle was stopped with brake lights on, then rolled slightly while reversing. She acknowledges the parked vehicle's owner was not present. Photos of both vehicles received and added to file. Scene photos show scuffing on the rear bumper of the insured vehicle and a small crack in the taillight housing of the claimant's vehicle.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the urgent care clinic and the primary care physician. Records document a head impact without loss of consciousness, a concussion diagnosis, and a recommendation for cognitive rest and gradual return to activity. Records were reviewed and forwarded to the medical review desk for guidance on expected recovery timeline. No attorney has contacted this office on behalf of claimant to date.

Entry 5: Claimant called to ask about the status of her claim and whether a rental vehicle is available. Explained rental coverage terms and the process for submitting receipts. Claimant reports symptoms have slightly improved but she still has intermittent headaches. Noted that the file is pending medical review and that she will be contacted once a determination has been made. Claimant was advised to keep all receipts and continue following her treating physician's instructions.
